core_capabilities: Discover active venues, browse their submissions, and open a paper's metadata and PDF.
Read reviews and decisions associated with a paper and participate in its discussion.
As a reviewer, inspect assigned papers and submit or revise structured reviews with ratings and confidence.
As an area chair, monitor assigned papers, reviewer progress, ratings, and recorded decisions.
Add researchers to the venue's reviewer pool and assign or unassign papers using workload, affinity, bid, expertise, and conflict context.
secondary_capabilities: Search, sort, and paginate a venue's submission list.
Filter and sort replies within a paper's forum.
Export area-chair paper and review progress as a CSV file.
Browse researcher profiles, expertise, external profile links, and publications.

nodes.description: Filtered reviewer candidates for “Reward Model Ensembles for Robust RLHF Alignment” to under-capacity reviewers matching Elena Popov.
Filtered the NeurIPS 2025 submissions to the two papers authored by David Kim.
Filtered assigned papers to those with fewer than three reviewers and exported the resulting list.
Located the NeurIPS 2025 submission “Scaling Laws for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Language Models” and downloaded its PDF.

Posted an official comment on the sparse mixture-of-experts paper requesting clarification about diminishing returns beyond 128 experts when controlling for routing entropy and active parameters per token.
Searched for protein structure prediction and opened the forum page for “Geometric Flow Matching for Protein Structure Prediction.”
Opened the NeurIPS 2025 submissions and filtered them for "computer vision," showing the matching self-supervised visual representation learning paper.
Opened the NeurIPS 2025 conference and sorted all submissions by date in descending order.
Viewed Elena Popov's existing reviewer assignment details for “Geometric Flow Matching for Protein Structure Prediction.”
Searched for David Kim and opened his author profile showing his affiliation, expertise, external links, and recent publications.
Viewed the NeurIPS 2025 console links showing 3 Area Chair papers and 0 Reviewer assignments.
Viewed David Kim's “Reward Model Ensembles for Robust RLHF Alignment” submission, including its abstract and keywords.
Viewed the NeurIPS 2025 author information and submission deadline.
Viewed the NeurIPS 2025 submission “Efficient Attention via Learned Sparse Patterns for Long-Context Transformers,” which lists Aisha Patel as an author.
Viewed the NeurIPS 2025 Reviewer Console, which showed no papers assigned for review.
Aisha Patel was added to the NeurIPS 2025 reviewer pool.
James Liu was assigned as a reviewer for “Self-Supervised Visual Representation Learning via Multi-Scale Masked Autoencoders.”
The forum comments were filtered to Official Comment replies matching “token-routing entropy” and sorted oldest first.
An official comment asking about calibration and sensitivity of the uncertainty-aware PPO threshold was posted, and the replies were searched for that topic.
Viewed the area chair task list with assigned papers, submitted reviews, reviewer ratings, and awaiting-review statuses.
Viewed two submitted reviews for the sparse mixture-of-experts scaling laws paper, including their ratings, confidence levels, and critiques.
Assigned a third reviewer to “Efficient Attention via Learned Sparse Patterns for Long-Context Transformers,” completing the checklist item that all papers have three reviewers.
Exported the area chair's assigned papers and filtered the list to the Scaling Laws for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Language Models submission.
Filtered reviewer assignments for the selected paper to Aisha Patel and revealed a same-institution conflict.
David Kim was added to the NeurIPS 2025 reviewer pool and shown for Paper #1 with a same-institution conflict.
Priya Sharma was removed as a reviewer for “Scaling Laws for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Language Models.”
James Liu was unassigned from the self-supervised visual representation learning paper, reducing its assigned reviewers from three to two.
A third reviewer was assigned to the Geometric Flow Matching paper, and its reviewer pool was filtered for Priya Sharma with the below-capacity option enabled.
The reviewers for Paper #2 were sorted by bid.
Viewed submission 1 details, including its abstract and two submitted reviewer ratings and confidence scores.
Filtered the assigned papers list to show only “Scaling Laws for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Language Models.”
Filtered the reviewers for Paper #2 by “self-supervised learning,” showing Aisha Patel with a same-institution conflict.
The reviewers for Paper #2 were reordered by affinity score, showing Aisha Patel's same-institution conflict.
Priya Sharma was unassigned from Paper #3, reducing her review load from 5/5 to 4/5.
Viewed the area chair's three assigned papers with their submitted review and assignment statuses.
Viewed Priya Sharma's existing assignment, high bid, and recent co-author conflict for the Scaling Laws for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Language Models submission.
Expanded submission 5 to view its abstract and keywords.
Downloaded the PDF for assigned paper #5, “Efficient Attention via Learned Sparse Patterns for Long-Context Transformers.”
